Landing update for `a232fab538672f4cbf6ad4d62b5b73a1089259fb`: the PR-related failures were repaired and the final local proof passes 103 distinct tests, core/all 27 test-type graphs, scoped guards, and independent review.

The only originating failure in [run 36682289478](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36682289478/job/109780524249) is the unchanged emoji-avatar UI E2E test. The actual tested merge is `140e6058253bc68fcbfc4bc3a62b754ee1110ebe`, with ordered parents `108a7a16bd7cd251f154d4ca3d99baf906690ef6` and this PR head; its tree matches the computed merge. UI, harness, dependencies, and workflow inputs are identical to that main parent.

The timeout is at the **first bounded-emoji Save**, waiting for a browser-local `agents.update` capture. [The failed wait](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/140e6058253bc68fcbfc4bc3a62b754ee1110ebe/ui/src/e2e/avatar-initial-emoji.e2e.test.ts#L244-L254) uses [MockWebSocket rather than a real Gateway](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/140e6058253bc68fcbfc4bc3a62b754ee1110ebe/ui/src/test-helpers/control-ui-e2e.ts#L2806-L2831), so the changed backend plugin/runtime implementation does not handle this request. This is source/control-flow independence evidence—not a claimed same-case main failure reproduction or a diagnosed UI timing race. The 22 fail-fast-cancelled jobs remain incomplete coverage.

I retained the full checkout/failure/aggregate/cancellation logs and a native exception candidate, but its **read-only preflight refused**: `Prior-CI admin admission: writer must administer the target organization repository`. The managed `roboclaw-bot` writer is an organization member, not an organization admin. No merge, permission change, identity switch, or auto-merge re-arm was attempted.

@steipete, as the existing requested reviewer, could you adjudicate this source-independent UI failure and perform the permitted native exception if its evidence is sufficient? Other security/review requirements must still pass. The previous auto request is confirmed cancelled, and its retained recovery receipt is preserved for the replacement-head flow. This is a request for administrator action, not a claim that the exception has been admitted.

Post-close public-client proof for exact head `a232fab538672f4cbf6ad4d62b5b73a1089259fb`

**Result: passed.** After the lending Gateway closed, the surviving Gateway answered public `models.list` and completed real agent turns.

**Can this happen in a single-process deployment?** Not through `openclaw gateway`. The run loop serves one Gateway per process and closes it before it starts the next one ([close](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/a232fab538672f4cbf6ad4d62b5b73a1089259fb/src/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop.ts#L852-L861), [next start](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/a232fab538672f4cbf6ad4d62b5b73a1089259fb/src/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop.ts#L1278-L1285)). A second `startGatewayServer` call on the same state without a shared owner also cannot start: in my first attempt it waited 300 s, then failed with `GatewayLockError: failed to acquire gateway state ownership`. Two Gateways can only run side by side in one process if they share one Gateway state owner (`gatewayStateOwner`, the same option the CLI run loop passes). The proof below uses that setup. It is the closest real equivalent to the sibling-shutdown test.

**Setup**
- `pnpm build` of the exact head passed (5m 32s).
- One Node process imports the built `dist` `startGatewayServer`. It acquires one state owner and starts Gateway A, then Gateway B, on separate loopback ports with token auth.
- Everything runs in a throwaway `HOME`/`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` under `/private/tmp`. No live state or live Gateway was used.
- Model: `openrouter/openai/gpt-4.1-mini` through the bundled OpenRouter plugin with a real API key. The key was held only in the process environment.
- A local hook-only probe plugin (`llm_input`) records the ID of the module instance that serves each turn.
- Every request came from a separate process using the public WebSocket client (`pnpm openclaw gateway call <method> --url ws://127.0.0.1:<port> --token … --json`). The `agent` calls used `--expect-final`.

**Timeline** (instance → registering Gateway: `de3b0497` = A full, `2ae5a06a` = B full)

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `models.list` on A / B | ok; target model present (463 / 858 entries) |
| agent turn on A, before close | `status: ok`, reply = nonce; `llm_input` served by `2ae5a06a` (**B's instance**, so B is the lender) |
| agent turn on B, before close | `status: ok`, reply = nonce; served by `2ae5a06a` |
| `close()` lender B | clean shutdown in 149 ms; B's `readyz` listener gone. `2ae5a06a` disposed 20 ms into close, and a fresh `discovery` instance `7d1917fe` registered 6 ms later, before close returned |
| `models.list` on survivor A | ok, target model present (858 entries, 1.76 s) |
| agent turn on A, after close | `status: ok`, reply = nonce (3.4 s); served by `7d1917fe`. The closed lender's instance was not used |
| second `models.list` + agent turn on A | ok / `status: ok`, reply = nonce; still `7d1917fe` |
| final shutdown | `7d1917fe` and `de3b0497` disposed |

The Gateway logs showed no warnings or errors around the close. The other warnings were the expected provenance notice for the local unverified probe plugin (once per Gateway) and one `[gateway] update status failed to initialize: AbortError` line, both logged before the close.

**Maintainer decision (Ayaan, 2026-09-30): both lifecycle tradeoffs are accepted for landing at `a232fab538672f4cbf6ad4d62b5b73a1089259fb`.**

1. **Prepared turns use the admitting Gateway's full-mode registrations for unchanged plugins (borrowing).** Accepted. On main, a republish freezes the Gateway for 68–142 s and ends in 5/5 recovery restarts. This PR brings that down to about 1.3–1.5 s with 0 restarts. Unlike closed #160983, borrowing never shares module identity: a turn uses the Gateway's live instance or evaluates a fresh module.
2. **A long admitted turn can exceed the 60 s explicit-reload drain and leave the previous plugin instance serving.** Accepted. When the drain times out, the reload keeps the old instance serving, so the in-flight turn completes instead of failing. The operator sees the timeout error and can wait for the turn or cancel it.

The public post-close proof on this head is in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/161267#issuecomment-5907830560.

Landed as 6c9809acf1bd5a606907783f05ed0b6ecf5b748d (squash of exact head `a232fab5`).

- **Bug:** with large plugins installed, every model change made prepared runtimes capture another copy of each plugin. The Gateway froze for 68–142 s and ended in "recovery restart required".
- **Fix:** prepared runtimes borrow unchanged plugin instances from their admitting Gateway. The Gateway keeps custody of those instances, and recovery handles the case where the lending Gateway closes.
- **Proof:** republish took 0.6–1.4 s with 0 restarts, versus 68–142 s with 5/5 restarts on main. An installed release-to-candidate upgrade run passed. On this head, a public `models.list` and real agent turns succeeded after the lending Gateway closed (#issuecomment-5907830560).

The lifecycle tradeoffs were accepted in #issuecomment-5907833707. The single red CI job is the unrelated emoji UI e2e timeout (#issuecomment-5908179695); it was merged past with admin under the maintainer's standing approval. Thanks @roboclaw-bot for driving the ownership follow-ups and CI repairs.
